prompt: Write a Python function `solve_tsp(dist: list[list[int]]) -> tuple[list[int], int]` that solves the Traveling Salesman Problem for the distance matrix `dist` (a symmetric NxN matrix, dist[i][j] is the distance from city i to city j, 0-indexed). Return `(tour, total_distance)` where `tour` is a list of city indices that starts and ends at city 0 and visits every other city exactly once, and `total_distance` is the sum of distances along that tour. This instance has 11 cities -- brute-force permutation search is too slow to be practical here, so a real approach (dynamic programming / Held-Karp, or a solver such as OR-Tools) is expected. Find the SHORTEST possible tour -- the true optimum, not just any valid tour.
checker:
dist = [[0, 92, 115, 130, 81, 43, 54, 52, 163, 77, 170], [92, 0, 119, 76, 70, 187, 149, 110, 112, 63, 185], [115, 119, 0, 142, 161, 71, 62, 114, 79, 160, 98], [130, 76, 142, 0, 138, 79, 144, 125, 173, 88, 75], [81, 70, 161, 138, 0, 104, 93, 33, 96, 46, 36], [43, 187, 71, 79, 104, 0, 100, 120, 109, 149, 142], [54, 149, 62, 144, 93, 100, 0, 61, 81, 122, 92], [52, 110, 114, 125, 33, 120, 61, 0, 51, 18, 31], [163, 112, 79, 173, 96, 109, 81, 51, 0, 97, 106], [77, 63, 160, 88, 46, 149, 122, 18, 97, 0, 133], [170, 185, 98, 75, 36, 142, 92, 31, 106, 133, 0]]
n = len(dist)

tour, total = solve_tsp(dist)

assert tour[0] == 0 and tour[-1] == 0, f"tour must start and end at city 0, got {tour}"
assert sorted(tour[1:-1]) == list(range(1, n)), f"tour must visit every other city exactly once, got {tour}"

recomputed = sum(dist[tour[i]][tour[i + 1]] for i in range(len(tour) - 1))
assert recomputed == total, f"reported distance {total} does not match the actual tour distance {recomputed}"

# True optimum for this instance, verified in advance by exhaustive search
# over all 10! permutations offline -- too slow to redo on every check, and
# the point of a golden item is a known-correct answer to compare against,
# not a live recomputation.
TRUE_OPTIMUM = 620
assert total == TRUE_OPTIMUM, f"tour is valid but not optimal: got {total}, true optimum is {TRUE_OPTIMUM}"
print('OK: optimal tour found, distance', total)
